decision_conditions: <p><b>BREEAM – Pre-Occupation&nbsp;</b></p><p>No part of the development hereby approved shall be used or occupied until a Post-Construction Review Certificate issued by the Building Research Establishment or other equivalent assessors confirming that the non-residential development has achieved a BREEAM rating of not less than the standards equivalent to ‘Excellent’ has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.’&nbsp;</p><p><b>Reason:</b> To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources and to comply the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy CC2.6 of Merton’s Local Plan 2024.&nbsp;</p>

<p><span style="font-size: 11px;">NRMM</span></p><p><span style="font-size: 11px;">All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/</span></p><p><span style="font-size: 11px;">Reason: To manage and prevent further deterioration of existing low quality air across London in accordance with London Plan Policies SI1(B)(1c) and SI1(B)(2d).</span></p>

<p>No unit shall be occupied until the vehicle parking spaces associated with that unit have been laid out and made available for parking purposes in accordance with the approved plans. The parking spaces shall thereafter be retained for the parking of vehicles by occupiers and users of that unit and shall not be used for any other purpose.</p><p>Reason: To ensure the safety of pedestrians and vehicles and the amenities of the surrounding area and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies T4 and T7 of the London Plan 2021 and policy T16.4 of Merton Local Plan 2024.</p>

<p>Active and passive Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure shall be installed in accordance with approved Site Plan W063-CMP-SI-ZZ-DR-A-00100 (Rev PL1), which provides for 20 active EV charging points. The EV charging infrastructure associated with the parking spaces serving each individual commercial unit shall be installed and made available for use prior to the first occupation of that commercial unit. The infrastructure shall thereafter be retained and maintained for that purpose.</p><p><br></p>

<p>Prior to the first occupation of any unit, a Delivery and Servicing Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with TFL. The approved Plan shall be implemented upon the first occupation of that unit and shall thereafter be adhered to for the lifetime of the development.</p><p>Reason: To ensure the safety of pedestrians and vehicles and to safeguard the amenities of the surrounding area, in accordance with Policies T4 and T7 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy T16.4 of the Merton Local Plan 2024.</p>

<p><b>Whole Life Carbon Assessment -Pre-Occupation&nbsp;</b></p><p>&nbsp;Prior to the occupation of the development, the post-construction tab of the GLA’s Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment Template shall be completed in line with the GLA’s Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment Guidance. Together with any supporting information, the Whole Life Carbon Assessment shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.&nbsp;</p><p><b>Reason: </b>To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: Policy SI2 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CC2.6 of Merton's Local Plan 2024.</p><p><br></p>

Approved Plans - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: [insert plans]

Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning

<p style="text-align: justify; "><strong style="font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;;">Cycle Parking:</strong><span style="font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;;"> No unit shall be occupied until the cycle parking facilities associated with that unit, as shown on the approved plans, and in accordance with the approved Transport Statement dated&nbsp;</span><font face="Segoe UI">April 2026,</font><span style="font-family: &quot;Segoe UI&quot;;">&nbsp;have been provided and made available for use. The cycle parking facilities shall thereafter be retained and kept available for use by the occupiers and visitors of that unit at all times.</span></p><p style="text-align: justify; "><u>Reason</u>: To ensure satisfactory facilities for cycle parking
are provided and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for
Merton: policy T5 of the London Plan 2021 and policies T16.1 and T16.2 of the
Local Plan 2024.</p>

Commencement of development (Full Permission) - The development to which this permission relates shall be commenced not later than the expiration of 3 years from the date of this permission.

Reason:  To comply with Section 91 (as amended) of the Town & Country Planning Act 1990.

<p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; "><span style="line-height: 107%;"><u><span style="font-size: 14px;">Contaminated Land - Pre-liminary Risk Assessment, Site
Investigation and Remediation Method Statement </span></u><span style="font-size: 14px;">-&nbsp;</span></span><span style="font-size: 14px;">No development shall occur until:</span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 14px;">i) a preliminary risk-assessment has been submitted to and
approved in writing by the local planning authority.</span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify;"><span style="line-height: 107%;"><span style="font-size: 14px;">ii) a site-investigation has been conducted to consider the
potential for contaminated-land and has been submitted to and approved in
writing by the local planning authority.</span><o:p></o:p></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">











</span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify;"><span style="line-height: 107%; font-size: 14px;">iii) a remediation method statement, described to make the
site suitable for, intended use by removing unacceptable risks to sensitive
receptors, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning
authority.</span></p><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="line-height: 107%;"><o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify;"><span style="line-height: 107%;"><u><span style="font-size: 14px;">Reason</span></u><span style="font-size: 14px;">: In order to protect the health of future occupiers
of the site and adjoining areas in accordance with the following Development
Plan policies for Merton: policy SI 10 of the London Plan 2021 and policy D12.1
of the Local Plan 2024.</span></span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;line-height:107%;font-family:
" arial",sans-serif"=""><o:p><br></o:p></span></p>

<p class="MsoNormal"><b>NON-RESIDENTIAL CO2 REDUCTIONS – Pre-occupation</b></p><p class="MsoNormal">No part of the development hereby approved shall be used or occupied until evidence demonstrating that the development has achieved CO2 reductions in accordance with those outlined in the energy statement (Energy, Sustainability &amp; Overheating Statement. Dated 13.04.2026), has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.’&nbsp;</p><p class="MsoNormal">Reason: To ensure that the development achieves a high
standard of sustainability and makes efficient use of resources and to comply
with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: polices SI 2, SI 3 and
SI 5 of the London Plan 2021 and policies CC2.1, CC2.2, CC2.3, CC2.4, CC2.5 and
CC2.6 of the Local Plan 2024.<o:p></o:p></p>

<p><b>Non-domestic District Heating Networks – Pre-commencement&nbsp;</b></p><p>No development shall commence until evidence demonstrating that the development has been designed to enable connection of the site to an existing or future district heating network has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall be designed in accordance with the Technical Standards of the London Heat Network Manual (2021).’ The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.&nbsp;</p><p><b>Reason: </b>To demonstrate that the site heat network has been designed to link all building uses on site (domestic and non-domestic), and to demonstrate that sufficient space has been allocated in the plant room for future connection to wider district heating, in accordance with London Plan policies SI2 and SI3.&nbsp;</p><p><br></p>

<p>Drainage Maintenance and Management Plan - The development shall not be occupied until a maintenance and management plan for the implemented drainage system is submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>The approved plan shall be implemented for the lifetime of the development.</p>

<p>Lighting Strategy - Prior to first occupation of the development, an external lighting strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The strategy shall include details of the location, design, luminance levels, and hours of operation of all external lighting, and demonstrate measures to minimise light spill and glare to protect residential amenity, biodiversity, and the character of the area. The approved lighting shall be installed and operated in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter.</p><p>Reason: To ensure a high standard of design, and safeguard the amenities of the area and the occupiers of neighbouring properties and ensure compliance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D12.1 &amp; D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024.</p>

<p>Demolition and Construction Environmental Management Plan (DCEMP) -</p><p>Prior to the commencement of development, a detailed Demolition and Construction Environmental Management Plan (DCEMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The DCEMP shall</p><p>include:</p><p>a)Air Quality &amp; Dust Management Plan (AQDMP), based on the approved Air Quality Assessment. The AQDMP shall be in accordance with The "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG). The AQDMP will need to detail the measures to reduce the impacts during the construction phase.</p><p>b) Construction Management Plan (CMP) identifying:</p><p>-Hours of operation</p><p>-The parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors</p><p>- Loading and unloading of plant and materials</p><p>- Storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development</p><p>- The erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative</p><p>displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate</p><p>- Wheel washing facilities</p><p>- Measures to control and monitor the emission of noise and vibration during</p><p>construction</p><p>- demonstration to show compliance with BS5228</p><p>- measures to control the emission of dust and dirt during construction/demolition</p><p>- a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works The development shall not be implemented other than in accordance with the approved scheme, unless previously agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.</p><p>Reason: To ensure the safety of pedestrians and vehicles and the amenities of the surrounding area and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies T4 and T7 of the London Plan 2021 and policies T16.3 and T16.4 of Merton Local Plan 2024.</p>

﻿Drainage - Surface water from private land shall not discharge on to the public highway. Details of the drainage system for surface water drainage to prevent the discharge of surface water from private land on to the highway shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to commencement of works. Before any part of the development hereby permitted is first occupied, the surface water drainage system shall be completed in accordance with the approved details and shall be retained permanently thereafter.

Reason: To ensure satisfactory means of surface water drainage, to reduce the risk of flooding and to comply with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policy SI 13 of the London Plan 2021 and policies F15.7, F15.8 and F15.9 of the Local Plan 2024.

<p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; "><span style="font-size:12.0pt;line-height:107%;font-family:
" arial",sans-serif"=""><u><span style="font-size: 14px;">Boundary Treatment</span></u><span style="font-size: 14px;"> - The development shall not be occupied until details of all boundary walls or fences are submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall be implemented prior first occupation of the development.&nbsp;</span></span></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;line-height:107%;font-family:" arial",sans-serif;="" mso-fareast-font-family:aptos;mso-fareast-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-ansi-language:="" en-gb;mso-fareast-language:en-us;mso-bidi-language:ar-sa"=""><span style="font-size: 12pt; line-height: 107%;"><u><span style="font-size: 14px;">Reason</span></u><span style="font-size: 14px;">: To ensure a satisfactory and safe development in accordance with
the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D4 and D8 of the
London Plan 2021 and policies D12.1 and D12.3 of the Local Plan 2024</span><s></s></span></span></p>

<p>Hard and Soft Landscaping – No above ground works shall take place full details of both hard and soft landscaping works are submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The details shall include: </p><p>A) Hard landscape works:</p><p>1. Benches/seating, road markings or similar method of delineation and bollards</p><p>2. Porous Hard surfacing materials; </p><p>3. Proposed and existing utility services above and below ground (e.g. drainage, power, communications cables, pipelines etc, indicating lines, manholes, supports etc). </p><p><br></p><p>B) </p><p>Soft landscape works including: </p><p>1. Full Planting Plans in context with the development. </p><p>2. Written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment). </p><p>3.Plans and written specifications shall detail the quantity, density, size, species, position and the proposed time or programme of planting of all shrubs, hedges, grasses etc, together with an indication of how they integrate with the proposal in the long term with regard to their mature size and anticipated routine maintenance, especially over the first 2 years. </p><p>4.All tree, shrub and hedge planting included within that specification shall be carried out in accordance with BS 3936:1986 (parts 1, 1992, Nursery Stock, Specification for trees and shrubs, and 4, 1984, Specification for forest trees); BS 4043: 1989, Transplanting root-balled trees; and BS 4428:1989, Code ofpractice for general landscape operations (excluding hard surfaces). </p><p>Reason: To ensure a satisfactory standard of development in accordance with the following Development Plan policies for Merton: policies D4 and D8 of the London Plan 2021, policies D12.1 and D12.3 of Merton Local Plan 2024.</p>

<p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; ">Prior to the commencement of development, a construction level detail final scheme for the provision of surface and foul water drainage shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The drainage scheme will dispose of surface water by means of a sustainable drainage system (SuDS)&nbsp; limited to a greenfield rate of no more than 1.0 l/s in accordance with drainage hierarchy contained within the London Plan Policy (SI 12, SI 13 and SPG) and the advice contained within the National SuDS Standards. The require drainage details shall include:</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; ">a. Evidence that the proposed final solution will effectively manage the 1 in 30 &amp; 1 in 100 +40% allowance for climate change) storm events and 10% for urban creep during all stages of the development. The final solution should follow the principles set out in the drainage strategy. Discharge rates and storage volumes shall be provided using a maximum site wide discharge rate of 4.0 l/s.</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; ">b. Detailed drainage design drawings and calculations to include: a finalised drainage layout detailing the location of drainage elements, pipe diameters, levels, and long and cross sections of each element including details of any flow restrictions and maintenance/risk reducing features (silt traps, inspection chambers etc.).</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; ">c. A plan showing exceedance flows (i.e. during rainfall greater than design events or during blockage) and how property on and off site will be protected from increased flood risk.</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; ">d.Details of drainage management responsibilities and maintenance regimes for the drainage system.</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify; ">e. Details of how the drainage system will be protected during construction and how runoff (including any pollutants) from the development site will be managed before the drainage system is operational.</p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify;"><span style="line-height: 107%;"><u><span style="font-size: 14px;">Reason</span></u><span style="font-size: 14px;">: To ensure satisfactory means of surface water
drainage, to reduce the risk of flooding and to comply with the following
Development Plan policies for Merton: policy SI 13 of the London Plan 2021 and
policies F15.7, F15.8 and F15.9 of the Local Plan 2024.</span></span><o:p></o:p></p><p style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size:12.0pt;line-height:107%;font-family:" arial",sans-serif;="" mso-fareast-font-family:aptos;mso-fareast-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-ansi-language:="" en-gb;mso-fareast-language:en-us;mso-bidi-language:ar-sa"=""><br></span></p>

<p style="text-align: justify; "><span style="line-height: 107%;"><u><span style="font-size: 14px;">Construction Logistics Plan</span></u><span style="font-size: 14px;"> - Prior to the commencement of the
development hereby permitted, including demolition, a Construction Logistics
Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority in consultation with TFL.&nbsp; The approved measures shall
be adhered to throughout the construction process, unless the prior written
approval of the Local Planning Authority is first obtained to any variation.</span></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="text-align: justify;"><span style="line-height: 107%;"><u><span style="font-size: 14px;">Reason</span></u><span style="font-size: 14px;">: To ensure the safety of pedestrians and vehicles
and the amenities of the surrounding area and to comply with the following
Development Plan policies for Merton: policies T4 and T7 of the London Plan
2021 and policies T16.3 and T16.4 of the Local Plan 2024.</span></span><o:p></o:p></p>

<p>No demolition or development shall take place until a stage 1 written scheme of investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, and the programme and methodology of site evaluation and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works.</p><p><br></p><p>If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by stage 1 then for those parts of the site which have archaeological interest a stage 2 WSI shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the stage 2 WSI, no demolition/development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed stage 2 WSI which shall include:</p><p><br></p><p>A. The statement of significance and research objectives, the programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works</p><p><br></p><p>B. Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits</p><p><br></p><p>C. The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication &amp; dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the stage 2 WSI.</p><p><br></p><p>Reason:&nbsp;The application site is located within a Tier II Archaeological Priority Area, and to comply with NPPF Section16 and London Plan policy HC1.&nbsp;</p>
